description: Beeswarm plot: each of 43 countries is a dot placed by its share of households owning at least one dog (top row) or cat (bottom row), with the median country marked and Australia highlighted. Based on the Vega beeswarm example.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone the words are split into shorter lines.

text.signal: narrow ? ['Australia stands out', 'most for dogs'] : 'Australia stands out most for dogs'

subtitle.signal: narrow ? ['Each dot is one of 43 countries, placed by', 'its share of households with a dog or a cat'] : 'Each dot is one of 43 countries, placed by its share of households owning at least one dog (top row) or cat (bottom row)'

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".

scales.x: Turns a percentage into a left-to-right position: 5% at the left edge of the dot area, 55% at the right edge.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
usermeta.readingNote: Australia stands further above the typical country for dogs than cats. Different survey methods limit close country comparisons.
usermeta.clickSelection: story-interactions.js pins a main-mark selection in pinnedKey and clears it on an empty-space click. Species hues, quantitative colours, symbol areas and plotted positions retain their meanings.

signals.name: colorPetDogs
signals.description: Colour: the colour for dogs (amber). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-dogs in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetCats
signals.description: Colour: the colour for cats (plum). This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-pet-cats in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Colour: light grey, used for gridlines, empty squares and places with no data. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorSurface
signals.description: Colour: white, the colour of the card each chart sits on. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-surface in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: True below 680 pixels of available width. Use smaller dots and taller packing rows; annotations retain their own lines.

signals.name: radius
signals.description: How big each country dot is (its radius in pixels): smaller on a phone so all 43 dots still fit.

signals.name: plotLeft
signals.description: Where the dots may start from the left: a 70-pixel margin on a computer, none on a phone. The words "Dogs" and "Cats" sit above their rows on every screen.

signals.name: rowHeight
signals.description: Height reserved for each swarm, separated from the two annotation lines above it.

signals.name: rowDogs
signals.description: The middle line of the dog row: dog dots gather around this height.

signals.name: rowCats
signals.description: Cat-row centre; the extra inter-row gap reserves room for the reading note above the cat headings.

signals.name: plotHeight
signals.description: How tall the area with the dots is: both rows plus a little gap.

signals.name: legendY
signals.description: A dedicated legend line below the numeric axis and its title.

signals.name: legendX
signals.description: Legend entries start at the left of their dedicated line below the plot.

signals.name: height
signals.description: Plot, axis and dedicated legend line. The reading note sits between the two species rows.

signals.name: hoverIso
signals.description: Hovered country shared with the world map. Its dog dot becomes amber and its cat dot plum, and both enlarge. Other dots, including Australia, become grey. Mouseout restores default fills and sizes.

signals.name: selectedCountry
signals.description: Country chosen with the keyboard-accessible page dropdown.

signals.name: focusIso
signals.description: Pinned selection takes precedence over hover and the page-control selection.

signals.name: colorPage
signals.description: Plain annotation background, supplied by --color-page in css/style.css.

signals.name: readingLines
signals.update: wrapChartText(['Australia stands further above the typical country', 'for dogs than cats. Different survey methods limit', 'close country comparisons.'], min(300, width - 40), 12, fontBody)
signals.description: Wrap a note capped at 300 pixels. Each source line has at most ten words and sixty characters; wrapping can only shorten it.

signals.name: pinnedKey
signals.description: Main-mark selection pinned by a click. Empty chart space clears it; the loader preserves it across responsive redraws.

signals.name: activeCountry
signals.description: Pinned selection takes precedence over temporary hover.

data.name: countries
data.description: The survey numbers: one row per country per pet, with the share of homes that own one.

transform.description: Two country names are shortened in the survey file. This writes them out in full words.
transform.expr: {'Rep. of Moldova': 'Republic of Moldova', 'Bosnia & Herzegovina': 'Bosnia and Herzegovina'}[datum.country] || datum.country

transform.description: Copy the percentage into a shorter field name, "value".
Rank the countries from highest to lowest, separately for dogs and for cats (1 = highest).
Default fill: Australia uses the row species colour; other countries use grey.

data.name: medians
data.description: The "typical country" for each pet: the middle value when all 43 countries are lined up from lowest to highest.

transform.description: Find the middle value (median) of all countries, once for dogs and once for cats.

data.name: rows
data.description: The two rows of the chart: dogs and cats.

data.name: legend
data.description: Highlighted dog observations are amber and cat observations plum; other countries are grey.

transform.description: Use the CSS species colours for highlighted dots and grey for comparison countries.

data.name: axisTicks
data.description: The percentages written along the bottom (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%).

data.name: packedCountries
data.description: Calculate positions separately from dot appearance, so hovering cannot restart packing. Width changes recompute percentage positions before packing.

transform.description: Pack countries vertically with x fixed to each reported percentage. Only layout inputs restart packing; hover changes mark appearance downstream.

data.name: australiaLabelTops
data.description: Find the highest nearby dot in each species row so Australian percentage labels do not cover neighbouring dots.

marks.name: plot
marks.description: The box that holds the dots. Anything outside it is cut off, because a dot pushed past the edge would otherwise make the whole chart shrink.

axes.description: Faint upright gridlines at each percentage, to help you read where a dot sits. No line, ticks or words here; the words are drawn separately underneath.

marks.description: A dashed upright line in each row at the typical (median) country.
Median labels occupy the first annotation line, above the swarm marks.
marks.name: medianLabels
dots
marks.description: One dot per country per pet, with x fixed at the reported percentage. Australia uses the row species colour by default. Hover transfers that colour to the hovered country and increases its dot areas by 50%; other countries become grey. Packing retains the base radius.

fill.signal: activeCountry ? (activeCountry === datum.iso3 ? (datum.species === 'Dogs' ? colorPetDogs : colorPetCats) : colorBorder) : datum.colour

tooltip.signal: {'Country': datum.country, 'Pet type': datum.species, 'Households owning this pet': format(datum.value, ',') + '%', 'Survey data year': datum.data_year, 'Rank among selected countries': datum.rank}

marks.name: ausLabels
marks.description: Australian percentage labels sit directly above their dots, moving upward just enough to clear nearby points in dense layouts. Labels omit the country name and retain a six-pixel gap above the highest nearby dot.

y.signal: min(datum.y, data('australiaLabelTops')[0].species === datum.datum.species ? data('australiaLabelTops')[0].top : data('australiaLabelTops')[1].top) - sqrt(datum.size / PI) - 6

marks.description: Species names sit in each annotation heading, outside the packed dots.
marks.name: rowLabels

marks.description: The percentages under the dots. On a phone, 20% and 40% are hidden so the numbers do not crowd.
The axis title under the percentages: "Share of households owning at least one".

text.value: Share of households owning at least one

marks.description: Legend symbols show dog amber, cat plum and comparison grey.
Direct legend labels identify dog, cat and comparison symbols.

marks.name: beeswarmReadingNote
marks.description: A compact reading note in the empty gap between dog dots and the cat-row headings. Lines contain at most ten words and sixty characters.

marks.name: beeswarmReadingBackground
marks.description: Plain background follows the note text bounds, masking gridlines without a border or shadow.
